LESSON: LANGUAGE USE 7.3.1 SIMPLE PAST TENSE (ADDING -ED/- D)

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade one
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE ACTIVITIES
Strand: Strand 7
Topic 7.3: Language Use 7.3.1 Simple past tense (adding -ed/- d)
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Language Use 7.3.1 Simple past tense (adding -ed/- d), part of Strand 7 in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade one ENGLISH LANGUAGE ACTIVITIES.

Key inquiry question: How did you keep the compound clean last week?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Language Use 7.3.1 Simple past tense (adding -ed/- d) together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Learning to learn- Learning independently is enhanced as the learners practise using verbs in simple past tense to express what they did in the

past.

• Communication and collaboration – Learner’s ability to communicate clearly is enhanced as they use appropriate language structure to respond

to questions related to the theme.

Values:
Respect: Learners appreciate each other’s opinion as they engage in language games.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Life skills (self-esteem): Learner’s esteem is nurtured as they use simple past tense confidently in day- to -day communication.

Link to other learning areas

Comparative expressions of simple past tense are emphasised in Kiswahili Language Activities.

Suggested learning resources

• Audio, video clip

• Textbooks in braille and appropriate font and colour contrast
